description: A beautiful witch sets off on her adventure astride a broomstick. The crimson sky, sun shaped like an eye, and branches clawing like talons hint at lurking dangers ahead — yet her face radiates ease and confidence, the fearless spirit of the traveler. The open suitcase at her side holds her witch's journal, marking her as a witch of some experience, though the suitcase left ajar betrays her careless, wide-eyed nature. The black cat glances back, as if trying to warn her of the unknown risks ahead.

The Magician raises her staff with her left hand toward the heavens, unleashing wondrous magic, while her right index finger points to the earth — she is the bridge between above and below. Crystal ball, dagger, wand, and potion bottle float around her, drawn by the magic radiating from her being. She strides forward, confident and resolute, parting overlapping rose thickets whose thorns cannot touch her. The hat atop her head curls into the infinity symbol, the endless source of her boundless power.

A composed and introspective witch sits upright upon a stone pillar, head gently bowed over her magical tarot book. Beside her stand two owl sculptures — one black, eyes open, bearing the letter B for Boaz, meaning 'to bear and establish'; one white, eyes closed, bearing J for Jachin, meaning 'inner strength.' Together they form the Pillars of Truth, symbol of duality. Behind them, a shelf of books represents wisdom; moonlight through the glass reveals patterns — sun and lily above, pomegranate and palm below. In the distance, a crescent moon hangs quietly over a shimmering lake.

The magnificent Empress reclines with self-assured grace against her sofa. Her veil is embroidered with twelve hexagram stars representing the twelve zodiac signs. In her left hand she holds a magic pipe — emblem of power — curling smoke that lifts a red orb like the Earth; her right hand strokes a cat with maternal tenderness. Two cats, one black, one white, are drawn to her, nuzzling close. Behind her, a framed painting of forest and river gives life to branches that spill from the canvas, spreading across walls and floor — the earth awakening, vibrant and alive.

The handsome Emperor wears a crown of stars and a red flowing robe, standing with supreme confidence upon the back of a great dragon. The outer robe is embroidered with sun and mountain patterns, expressing his outward passion and strength; the inner lining bears moon and waves, concealing the love and tenderness within. His armor speaks of iron discipline. A crystal ball floats above his left palm, revealing within it a crest of shield, sword, and dragon. The cross in his right hand blazes with fierce light, symbol of life and sovereign power.

A mysterious witch wears a triple crown, her brow marked with the scepter pattern of mastery. Her veiled eyes are downcast, gazing upon the figure in her palm; her lips barely part as if whispering secret knowledge. At her throat, two crossed keys — the moment to unlock the doors of wisdom and mystery. On her ring fingers she wears Y-shaped (Taurus) rings, fingers pointing heavenward in blessing. In her hands stand disciples who heed her teachings: one offering roses on the left, the other white lilies on the right.

A pair of lovers in love dance among the clouds. An angel bows her head, cradling a crescent moon in her hands; she breathes a gentle wisp of smoke that weaves between the lovers. The wing-shaped galaxy bears five red stars on the left for the five senses, and twelve orange stars on the right for the twelve zodiac signs. The man wears a wizard's hat and robes, clasping his lover's hand tightly; a small serpent-shaped hairpin holds the woman's flowing hair.

A powerful witch wears a double-headed magic hat, an eight-pointed star gleaming amid laurel leaves. Blue draperies fall from the hat brim, starlight glimmering through. One hand propping her chin, the other holding her staff, she surveys the chessboard below with proud confidence. Two griffin pieces — one black, one white — lock their gaze on the Emperor opposite; victory seems within reach. The bats behind her, her familiars, flutter with restless excitement at the coming triumph.

A girl in a white gown stretches her body with ease, her posture relaxed and her expression serene — as though everything bends to her will. Her left hand gently soothes the head of a lion rearing forward with bared fangs. Flowers blooming from her chest wind into her braid, forming the inverted figure-eight of infinity, and together with her hand they hold the fierce lion in perfect stillness.

The silent night sky, still as deep water. A hermit who has climbed to the summit leans upon her staff, head bowed in contemplation. The world around her is desolate and apart; before her shines the Lantern of Wisdom, its hexagram star radiating the light of the subconscious, illuminating the path ahead.

The great Wheel of Fortune spins endlessly among the stars. Leo, Taurus, Scorpio, Aquarius and more gleam in its wake. The outermost irregular ring represents invisible creative force; a white serpent descends along the ring. A wise witch wielding a staff sits enthroned above it. The middle ring, representing formative power, is becoming a complete circle; a jackal races ever upward. At the bottom lies the Earth — the material world. All life is caught in the inescapable current of fate.

Unlike the Justice of old, this is a witch of swift and decisive righteousness. A cold golden mask covers her eyes. Her right hand holds a sword, ready to charge forward and deliver judgment at any moment; her left hand raises high, magic suspending the scales above her head. A black crow and a white dove each tug at her advancing steps. A ribbon winds about her waist, inscribed with the ancient Roman legal maxim: 'Fiat justitia, ruat caelum — Let justice be done, though the heavens fall.'

A witch bound to a cross as green flames consume her body — yet even in the fire she remains utterly serene. The broken shackles on her wrists reveal that she could free herself if she wished; she simply hasn't yet decided to. Behind her, a flock of white doves rises up through the flames — the body may be bound, but nothing can contain her lofty ideals and the deeper pursuit of her spirit.

The black-veiled Death walks through the waters of the River Styx, her right hand trailing across the surface, the ripples drawing the boundary between life and death. Some candles in the water have gone out; others flicker on with quiet tenacity. Death's shadow brings the arrival of endings; but in the distance a new dawn rises, kindling the hope of life. Life and death endlessly transform upon this card.

The wings of an angel spread behind the witch. A square-and-triangle pendant at her throat grants her the power of the elements. She lightly waves her wand, and two potion bottles glide back and forth under its direction, maintaining a living balance. She brews her potion — as if preparing the elixir of new life for the Death card that came before. The card's verdant, natural atmosphere breathes tranquility and peace.

The demon Lilith gazes down with contemptuous amusement at the skulls kneeling before her, desire having grown horns upon their heads. The one with a fruit-tail on the left is a woman; the one with a flame-tail on the right is a man. Both reach upward, pleading to the demon — they are Eve and Adam, cast into the underworld for stealing the forbidden fruit. The chains upon them are the shackles of their own craving. The Devil embodies the fall into materialism and desire; the inverted pentagram is its signature symbol.

The great magic monolith standing atop the mountain peak is struck by a divine magic circle descending from the heavens — split in two. Thunder shatters the surroundings; bats scatter in all directions. This is a sudden, harrowing magical confrontation. Against such overwhelming force, all resistance is futile; one can only surrender to this moment of upheaval. The Tower's archetype is the Tower of Babel, built by humanity and destroyed as divine punishment. The lightning from the sky is the language of that judgment — catastrophe strikes without warning, heralding a dark and turbulent season.

A witch gently cradles a glowing eight-pointed star, its warm light radiating outward. Sheer white veil drapes her form. Her silken hair flows into two streams — the left one, the water of life, flows into a lake; the right one divides into five streams representing the five senses, one stream flowing back into the lake to replenish the magical wellspring of the subconscious. Seven small stars ring the scene. A quiet, healing stillness drifts between mountain and water.

In the dim, haunting night, a witch gazes upward with unease at a blood-red moon. Within the moon, an eye rises slightly, watching. Fear and confusion ripple outward to the white cat and black serpent below. Even the surrounding branches close in like pale bones, deepening the card's dread and bewilderment.

A bright, sunny golden-haired little witch stands happily on her broomstick, magic wand pointing forward. Sunflowers blaze in full bloom, doves soar freely on the breeze, and the golden sun hangs in the blue sky like a great sunflower in flower — its single eye gazing warmly at the witch before it.

The barren mountain turns green once more. A golden-haired witch whose ears have become angel's wings bows her head, pouring every drop of her spirit into the conch shell in her hands. She sounds the horn, and butterflies — symbols of rebirth — flutter forth on its note. The music drifts between heaven and earth, nourishing all things in silence, releasing humanity from the confines of the material world and healing body and soul.

A white cat watches its witch with elegant poise as the crown is placed upon her magic hat, marking the glorious completion of her magical adventure. The clock in the shape of a zero witnesses the entire journey — the close of this chapter and the beginning of the next. A new cycle begins. The power of the four elemental planets orbits the witch, absorbed and transformed by her, proof that her trials too have come to their perfect fulfillment.

From the heart of the flames, a strong and powerful hand reaches out, the fire-element symbol tattooed on its middle finger, amplifying the energy of fire along with the flame patterns. White birds follow the direction of the fire upward, flying toward the sun.

The mage stands upon a city wall. One staff is planted on the wall; the other is held in hand. He gazes into the distance, a globe-shaped magic orb in his grip — as though suggesting that the world is not enough for him and he is already planning his next magical expedition.

A slender witch stands at the mountaintop, staff in hand. The two staffs planted in the ground show that her magic has already taken firm root. She gazes into the distance where a golden radiance shimmers, seemingly rich with great magical power, calling her forward to a journey of further training and greater achievement.

At the witches' gathering, four staffs stand like the pillars of a festival hall. Fireworks of celebration light the dark night; the witches have dressed in their finest, coming together to mark this special moment, their faces lit with joy and happiness.

Mages of different ages and walks of life clash under the influence of the fire element. Five magic staffs tangle and wrestle in midair — the whole scene a vivid picture of rivalry, conflict, and fierce competition.

A magical girl raises her victory staff high, riding atop a great parrot that carries the laurel crown of triumph in its beak. Five staffs stand behind her as if rallying to her side in celebration. The whole scene overflows with the joy and glory of triumph.

The witch grips her staff tightly in both hands, her gaze steely. The power of magic and blazing fire send her hair flying — it speaks of her full-hearted courage and determination, ready to meet the challenges and difficulties that stand before her.

Eight magic staffs move as one, slicing through the air at speed, tips pointing downward, about to reach the earth — nothing can halt their flight. This may also represent the swift relay of messages and the rapid unfolding of action.

The wounded witch grips her staff tightly; eight staffs stand erect, blocking her path. Bandages are wrapped around her head and hand — she has not yet recovered from her injuries — yet she chooses to take up her weapon again and hold her last position.

In the heart of the roaring fire, the mage furrows her brow and labors under the weight of ten staffs that look light but press down with the weight of mountains. Exhausted but still pressing forward. This crushing burden represents responsibility and pressure, reminding us that we sometimes need to set things down to recover our lightness.

The Page of Wands waves the staff and at once flames and sparks appear. The backdrop is desert; on his veil is the salamander totem of the wands family. Some salamanders' mouths do not connect to their tails, symbolizing actions or plans not yet brought to completion.

The Knight of Wands rides a griffin, holding his staff with bold self-assurance. His cloak bears the salamander pattern — but the mouth and tail do not connect, symbolizing an action or plan still in progress. This charge-forward knight is fully ready to embrace the next adventure.

The Queen of Wands wears a crown of leaves and gold; she sits upon her throne with confident ease. Her left arm cradles sunflowers, symbols of brightness and joy; her right hand holds the staff. Beneath her seat the pattern of a black cat is carved, representing her hidden power. The Queen's aura is formidable — full of passion and vitality.

The King holds the staff in his left hand, seated on the throne with his body leaning slightly forward — always ready to set out. The salamander pattern on the back of his throne, which had a broken tail on the Knight's card, is now a complete salamander, symbolizing the full completion of plans and actions. The King, with all his commanding force, is the fire element at its most fully realized.

From the magic flask, five streams of water gush forth — one for each of the five human senses. The water lily, a plant that thrives in deep water, suggests the pool below has great depth, symbolizing an abundance of emotion. A hand grasps the flask, its wrist marked with moon, sun, and water-element symbols, speaking of boundless inner energy.

The witch and the mage face each other, each holding a magic flask, touching them together in a toast. The potion that flies between them takes the shape of a heart in the air; warmth and affection bloom between them. Floating at the center is a lion-headed staff wrapped with two serpents — the lion's head and wings speak of love and beauty, while the twin-serpent caduceus represents communication and connection.

The witches' gathering has begun again. Three witches huddle around the cauldron, each drawing out her own potion to blend into the brew, their faces alight with joyful smiles — reunions are always the sweetest moments. Each witch wears different garb and a hat pinned with a different plant, showing their individual skills and independence. The three stand in a circle, honoring one another as equals with no hierarchy, sharing freely.

A magic apprentice sits with arms folded and eyes closed in rest — so long resting that cobwebs have settled on her. The three magic flasks on the table represent her past experience. A spider descends, carrying one more flask — echoing the very first card — a symbol of new opportunity, yet the apprentice does not see it.

At the bottom of the sea, a witch tattooed on the shoulder with Scorpio hugs herself and weeps. Three empty magic flasks represent the sorrows of the past. On the surface above float two flasks still filled with potion — the possible future still awaiting her. If only she can gather herself, everything can begin again.

In a warm magical greenhouse, a witch sits in the water of a pool and gently teaches her young apprentice. She tips the potion from the flask in her hand, and a seedling of hope shoots up in an instant. Five more star-shaped magic flasks surround them, all symbols of happy, golden times.

The mage, cradling a star-and-moon talisman, drifts into sleep. Seven chalices filled with different things drift around: a key for adventure, jewels for wealth, a laurel crown for victory, a bat for fear, a human skull, a heart for one's own magical spirit, and a serpent for wisdom. The vague, half-seen waves hint that all of this is nothing but a daydream.

The witch mounts her broomstick and flies away from the eight magic flasks she worked so hard to collect, in search of the empty ninth cup. Her red hair speaks of drive and action — the very theme of this card: abandonment, breaking the routine with decisive movement.

At the celebration, a Gemini witch proudly displays the nine magic flasks arrayed before her, surrounded by streamers and bobbing skull balloons. Her expression is triumphant, as if narrating exactly how she came to gather all of these. She is fully satisfied with where she is — a portrait of simple, uncomplicated contentment and delight.

A loving couple and the little cat they have taken in nestle together in happiness. Behind them, a joyful fountain sprays; flowers of happiness bloom all around; a rainbow arches across the horizon; ten potion flasks are arrayed in perfect completion above. The entire scene breathes harmony and peace — a feeling of full satisfaction and pure joy.

The Page of Cups is a gentle young boy who cradles a dolphin in his arms, symbolizing his tender sensitivity and deep empathy. When the potion is poured from the flask, the fish all gather to absorb its nourishment — and the fish represent imagination, further suggesting that this page possesses extraordinary creative vision.

The graceful knight rides a seahorse, advancing with quiet elegance. He holds up the potion flask and gazes into it with a dreamy, faraway look. The dolphin following behind represents imagination, creativity, and spirit; the fabric of his garments is patterned with ocean waves.

The Queen of Cups sits upon a shell at the edge of the sea. Unlike the King who floats on the waves in isolation, she sits on land — a sign of her closeness to people. She holds the potion flask tenderly, gazing at the dolphin inside with warm, affectionate eyes. Rich in water-element energy, gentle waves have become the very pattern of her skirt.

In the surging heart of the sea, the King of the Waters sits upon his throne, clad in a blue inner robe — the color of the water element, of imagination and creativity. He holds a potion flask and a lotus staff. A dolphin leaps from the waves, and to his right a sailboat appears — the subconscious surfacing. His success is a union of imagination, discipline, and determination; the steadiness of his gaze speaks of self-mastery that enables him to succeed again and again.

The crescent-moon hilt of the sword is carved with laurels of victory; the sharp crown pierces the sky like a blade, as if able to cut through to the very nature of this world. A witch's hand, charged with magic, reaches through the wind and grips the sword true and straight. Runes of the wind element are written on the hand; a serpent of wisdom coils around it — the power of intellect and clear-sighted reason made manifest.

A crescent moon hangs high on the horizon; beneath it, hidden currents stir and ice formations rise. Twin girls in white dresses stand back to back, hands clasped together, their expressions conflicted — both blindfolded with white cloth. The one on the left wears wind-element earrings in her ordinary-girl form; the one on the right wears Libra earrings with blackened nails, already transformed into a witch. The two swords crossed before them differ too — one a sword, one a magic blade — reflecting their inner conflict and the impossible difficulty of making a choice.

A heartbroken witch weeps tears of blood; her body transforms into brilliant crystal. Three sharp swords pierce through her heart, and the crystal cracks in an instant, blood trickling out like threads of silk. Dark clouds mass all around; anguish and sorrow pour down with the rain.

Three swords hang from the canopy above the bed. A woman warrior is resting, lying half-slumped on the pillow — but the battle-robe she has not yet removed, and the dagger still in her hand, tell us this is only a brief respite. She looks ready to spring up and fight at any moment.

The red-haired witch wears a look of smug satisfaction. Two swords are plunged into the ground; three more are in her hands — all trophies of her victory. The defeated party, shoulders slumped and retreating in the distance, tells us this turbulent struggle has only just ended. Dark clouds fracture in the far sky; the night is deep and shadowed. This victory may not be as complete as the red-haired witch imagines.

A full moon hangs at the horizon; night shimmers like water and a mood of sadness pervades everything. The witch sits in a boat carved of shining crystal moon-stone, poles it away toward the far distance. Six swords are thrust into the hull; the boat is cracked and fractured — pull out the swords and it would likely split apart. The churning water behind is the turmoil of the past; the broad, still waters ahead promise a calmer emotional future. Healing takes time.

A cowboy witch steals silently into the enemy camp and, catching them off guard, walks off with five swords — confident and undetected. The two swords she left behind symbolize the risk in this gambit; her abilities have limits, and she cannot face her enemy openly, so she resorts to cunning and deception to get what she wants. The crescent moon grinning in the sky above makes clear that this is no honorable act.

A witch in a blood-red gown stands with her back to us; her long black hair coils like shackles around her hands. As her head turns, we see that her eyes are covered by a red butterfly. Eight swords are planted all around her like sentinels; she appears helpless and trapped. But she is not truly bound — the moment she decides to take a step forward, she will be free.

The witch sits on the bed, covering her face in despair — just woken from a nightmare, or perhaps unable to sleep at all for worry and fear. The lamp has fallen, extinguished on the bed. Nine bloody swords hang on the wall, blood trailing from the tips, as if they have run her through from behind, pressing down on her with dread. A strange great moth with four black eyes floats in the air — a warning from the subconscious.

Eight swords pierce the witch's body; two more pass through her chest — the last two are the fingernails of a pair of giant hands below. Threads of blood trail down the pale skin — a sight that strikes the heart. And yet: far away at the edge of the dark sky, the first light of dawn is breaking. Even the darkest times of a life will eventually pass.

The Page of Swords is a sharp-minded young person full of curiosity. One hand grips a sword; he turns to look ahead, his hair flying in the wind along with the distant trees. Butterflies drift through the scene with untroubled freedom.

The short-haired Knight of Swords wears a solemn expression, clad in armor and a red cloak. One hand grips the sword; the other pulls the reins as the horse charges at full gallop through the howling wind.

The Queen of Swords wears a sharp crown; the butterfly pattern on her shoulders represents the soul and the wind element. She gazes with resolute calm at the upright sword in her hand — unwavering, impartial — symbolizing her power to cut through illusion, see the truth clearly, and bring exceptional insight and wisdom to bear.

The handsome golden-haired King of Swords sits with solemn dignity upon his throne. His expression is serious; his right hand holds the sword, blade tilted slightly to the right — the side of action. His left hand wears the ring of authority. The butterfly pattern decorating his cloak symbolizes the soul and the wind element; butterflies dance in the sky above him as well.

A mage's hand, tattooed with the earth-element symbol, floats in the air and holds a magic pentacle aloft. Below, plants burst into new bloom under the pentacle's influence. The pentacle is a connection to nature; behind it, green grass covers the hillside and a tree puts forth fresh buds. True to the Pentacles' practical spirit — the money and time you invest will bring great returns.

The mage rides a swallow through the air, effortlessly juggling two pentacles in hand. The coins are ringed by the figure-eight symbol; behind them, willow leaves sway in the breeze — symbols of the fluctuations of finance and the other currents of life.

In the halls of the magic academy, three mages stand before the great zodiac clock. Working together, the three pentacles are slowly, steadily finding their places. Each person carries her own role, which is what keeps the collaboration running smoothly. Judging by their focused expressions, it seems they are working together with real satisfaction.

The witch curls up on a rug, wearing a crown, surrounded by scattered gems, crystals, and pearls. The four most important pentacles are clutched tightly to her chest, her eyes fixed upon them with deep intensity, as if terrified of losing even the smallest sliver of what she has.

In the frozen waste, a ragged mage leans on his great white-cat companion, staggering forward. Warm light from inside falls across the church's stained-glass window; five pentacles happen to be cast across them in the light — yet they do not see it, hungry and cold, pushing on.

In the moonlight, the mage holds six pentacles with easy command, deciding with whom to share them. Below, two apprentices wait — for charity, or for lessons — but this power rests entirely in the mage's hands.

A little sprite in a straw hat, small sickle in hand, kneels beside a basket to rest, gazing longingly at the seven pentacles ripening before her. The sprite's vine grows lush and vigorous — proof of careful tending — and now she simply rests, waiting for the harvest to come in.

In a secluded mountain valley, the mage sits cross-legged, fully absorbed in practicing magic. Six perfect pentacles have already been completed; the one in hand is nearly there. Only the eighth remains to be filled with light and green energy. Cultivation requires walking the path one step at a time, steady and grounded.

An elegantly dressed witch stands with her back to us, contentedly admiring the pentacles arranged on the étagère before her — each one a trophy of persistent effort. Lush greenery surrounds her, the setting beautiful and serene, representing material abundance and pleasure. The bird at her side has chosen to forgo freedom just to remain close, symbolizing that behind this good life lies a great deal of endurance and sacrifice.

In the courtyard, grandmother witch holds her magic book and teaches the younger generation; even the white cat lingers nearby in curious companionship — a scene of warm, familial joy. Flowers and plants thrive all around; inside, the house is filled wall to wall with books. For a family of mages, this is surely the most precious wealth of all.

The Page of Pentacles is an eager young student. With a magnifying glass in one hand and a pentacle held in the other, raised to eye level, she gazes at the coin with careful, absorbed concentration, already lost in her research. The field around her is thick with greenery; hazy mountains rise in the distance.

The Knight of Pentacles sits astride a grand, regal black cat, examining the pentacle in his hand with careful attention. The black cat stands perfectly still, a pack on its back symbolizing experience and wealth. Of all four knight mounts, this is the only one at rest — reflecting a disposition of caution and pragmatism.

The Queen of Pentacles holds a pentacle aloft with both hands, head bowed in contemplation, seated at ease upon her tree throne. She sits beside a plant-rich streambank, surrounded by flowers and abundant foliage. A little rabbit — symbol of prolific abundance — keeps her company. The entire scene is peaceful and harmonious, rich in resources, and saturated with the feeling of earned prosperity.

The King of Pentacles is a ruler who has achieved all. Left hand holding a pentacle, right hand holding a staff, he sits with full confidence upon a throne shaped like a tree and decorated with ox bones, symbolizing material success and sovereign authority. Everything is within his command. Around him, grapevines and all manner of plants — the sign of great harvest — intertwine with him until man and nature are one.
